description: Deviations from the literal text of SPEC.md, with justification. A deviation is permitted ONLY when the literal text is unsatisfiable or strictly weaker than what it intends, and only when the intended content is proved in full. Every entry names the SPEC clause, what was changed, why, and the declaration that carries the intended strength. Silent deviation is forbidden. A deviation filed against a KERNEL-REFUTED clause is not a permanent resting place: SPEC.md is the normative contract, so a clause this repository has proved false is a defect in the contract and SHALL be corrected there. Entries whose `adoptedIntoSpec` names an amendment id have been so corrected; their refutation theorems stay cited, because the reason the text changed is part of the record and outlives the text it replaced. An amendment is the SMALLEST change that makes the clause true, never a restatement of a weaker theorem the repository happens to have; where the obligation nevertheless shrank, `strengthEffect` says so in those words.

deviations.refutedSpecText: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation
deviations.specText: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> (Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation /\ Wasm.CostedLabelling module invocation costedTrace)
deviations.issue: The literal biconditional is FALSE, and this is now PROVED rather than argued. `costedTrace` is universally quantified, and the right-hand side mentions it only through `eraseCosts costedTrace`, which is not injective: it discards the installed byte count of `enterGemm`, the requested page count of `memoryGrowSucceed`, and it identifies the whole ordinary-rule family in `Event.step`. A trace carrying forged cost labels whose erasure equals a valid plain trace therefore satisfies the right-hand side without being a costed run the machine can produce. The backward direction cannot hold for an arbitrary labelling.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.not_costed_erase_iff_plain_run -- for EVERY profile, not (forall module invocation costedTrace observation, CostedRun <-> Run (eraseCosts costedTrace))
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimalModule -- a module that passes `Wasm.validate` (minimalModule_validate), together with a three-step maximal run of it (minimal_finiteExecution)
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.forgedTrace -- [enterGemm 1, i32Const, returnGemm 0]; the run installs ZERO raw bytes, so the machine's label is `enterGemm 0`
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimal_run -- the right-hand side HOLDS of the forged trace
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.Counterexample.minimal_not_costedRun -- the left-hand side FAILS, under any profile
WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.erase_enterGemm_eq -- erasure discards the payload the two sides disagree about
deviations.resolution: RESOLVED AT THE FORMULA LEVEL BY AMENDING SPEC, not by deviating from it. SPEC 7.5 now states the biconditional with the minimal side condition `Wasm.CostedLabelling module invocation costedTrace` on the right-hand side, states the side-condition-free existential law `costed_run_iff_plain_run` beside it, and defines `CostedLabelling` -- a predicate the clause previously used without defining. The side condition is minimal in the sense that matters: it is a condition on LABELS alone (no observation, no store, no terminal status appears in it), so it cannot smuggle the conclusion into the hypothesis, and it is exactly the payload information `eraseCosts` discards. The existing `Wasm.costed_erase_iff_plain_run` carries that amended formula only for `Wasm.Subset.Module`; SPEC now fixes the public carrier as amended-Core `Wasm.Module`. Its binding is therefore WEAKER and the SPEC 15 name remains OUTSTANDING until the costed and plain semantics are migrated to the public carrier. This entry stays on file: the refutation is why the formula reads as it does.

deviations.refutedSpecText: A plan loop iterates a number of times determined by its extent. (SPEC 11.1 stated no rule for a register-bounded loop's trip count at all; the reading above is the one an implementer would take, and it is the one that breaks Plan.steps_le_stepBound.)
deviations.specText: A loop whose trip count is read from a register SHALL clamp that count at the profile's address-space ceiling (`Plan.loopRegMaxTrips = 2^32 - 1`, the released i32 ceiling, equal to `maxRawExtent`), so that a static step bound remains derivable from the plan text alone.
deviations.issue: An UNCLAMPED register-bounded loop would make the pre-existing theorem Plan.steps_le_stepBound FALSE: that theorem bounds executed steps by a static Nat computed from the plan text, and no fixed number bounds a loop whose trip count is an arbitrary register value (take body = setReg and an arbitrarily large extent register).
deviations.resolution: Plan.loopReg runs Nat.min (m.reg extentReg) loopRegMaxTrips times, with loopRegMaxTrips = 4294967295.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_trips_from_memory -- trip count IS the memory word, given n <= loopRegMaxTrips
WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_eq_loopNest -- agrees with the literal-extent form
WasmGemmGnaf.GNAF.loopReg_zero -- no clamp hypothesis needed
deviations.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH. loopRegMaxTrips is the released i32 ceiling and equals maxRawExtent, so the clamp is unreachable for any configuration the released ABI can present or any value the compiled i32 locals can hold. It preserves an existing theorem instead of weakening it. No SPEC 15 name is affected.
deviations.amendmentText: ADOPTED. SPEC 11.1 now states the clamp, names `Plan.loopRegMaxTrips`, records that it equals `maxRawExtent` and is therefore unreachable for the released ABI, and states that the trip count is still exactly the memory word below the ceiling.

deviations.refutedSpecText: theorem incremental_eq_full_rebuild (hupdate : (Atlas.accumulate budget state delta).result = .complete successor) : Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBody (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))
deviations.specText: theorem incremental_eq_full_rebuild (hcoherent : Atlas.Coherent state.body) (hupdate : (Atlas.accumulate budget state delta).result = .complete successor) : Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))
deviations.issue: The literal statement is FALSE, and this is PROVED, not argued. `state` is universally quantified over `Atlas.UnsealedState`, a type that carries neither a scope restriction nor a coherence obligation. (a) SCOPE: `Atlas.semanticRebuildBody` takes only the declaration base, which names no objective, profile or problem identity, so it always answers `Scope.unscoped`; `Atlas.semanticApplyBody` preserves the scope of the state it updates; `Atlas.canonicalize` copies the three identities verbatim. Any state whose objective identity is not `nullId` therefore falsifies the equation for EVERY budget and delta. (b) COHERENCE: a state may record a semantic half its declaration base does not derive, and the surplus survives canonicalisation.
refutedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild -- not (forall budget state delta successor, accumulate ... = complete successor -> canonicalize successor.body = canonicalize (semanticRebuildBody ...))
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_ne_full_rebuild_of_objectiveId -- the scope failure is systematic: it holds for every budget, delta and successor whenever state.body.objectiveId is not nullId
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.scopedState -- a COHERENT state (scopedState_coherent) in a scope of its own, on which the equation fails
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild_unscoped -- restricting SPEC's statement to unscoped states does NOT save it: the coherence hypothesis is doing work of its own
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.incoherent_ne_full_rebuild -- the witness for the line above: an UNSCOPED state that records one stray semantic object its empty declaration base does not derive
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.Counterexample.scopedState_accumulate -- the update instance used is `Delta.empty`, whose completion is itself required by SPEC 12.5's `update_empty_fixed_point`
deviations.resolution: RESOLVED BY AMENDING SPEC TO THE STRONGER FORM, not to the weaker theorem this repository already had. The obvious repair -- adding both hypotheses the refutations show to be load-bearing, `Atlas.Coherent state.body` AND `state.body.scope = Atlas.Scope.unscoped` -- is exactly the shape of `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` as declared in Atlas/Rebuild.lean, and adopting it would have amended SPEC to match a weaker theorem for a ledger point. It was REJECTED for that reason. SPEC 12.5 instead states the general form, which fixes the scope objection by rebuilding in the state's OWN scope rather than assuming it away: it implies the repaired literal form (instantiate the scope at `unscoped`) and additionally constrains every scoped state, about which the superseded text said nothing true. SPEC 12.5 now also requires `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact` (the same equation before canonicalisation, stronger again), `semanticApplyBody_coherent` and `rebuild_coherent`, so `Atlas.Coherent` is DISCHARGED at every state the pipeline produces rather than assumed, and it defines `Atlas.Coherent` and `Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith` in the clause's own fenced block. CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: the gap has reversed direction. SPEC now asks for MORE than the declaration named `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` proves. The proposition SPEC now asks for IS proved here, by `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_scoped`, but `xtask signature` credits a binding only when it is closed by `:= @<the SPEC name>`, so until the required name carries the amended proposition the binding stays AMENDED and the SPEC 15 name stays OUTSTANDING. The remaining action is a restatement of `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` in Atlas/Rebuild.lean as the scoped form; it was not made in the amending change, which owned SPEC.md, this file and the signature bindings only.
intendedContentProvedBy: WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_scoped -- canonicalize successor.body = canonicalize (semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations)); NO scope hypothesis
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact -- the same equation BEFORE canonicalisation, which is strictly stronger
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild -- SPEC's literal equation under the two necessary hypotheses
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.semanticApplyBody_coherent -- coherence is preserved by every update, so the hypothesis is discharged rather than assumed at every state the pipeline produces
WasmGemmGnaf.Atlas.rebuild_coherent -- and by the rebuild that starts a lifecycle
deviations.strengthEffect: STRENGTHENING RELATIVE TO THE SUPERSEDED TEXT, AND STILL NOT COUNTED. Nothing was given up: the coherence hypothesis cannot be dropped (`not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild_unscoped`) and the literal rebuild target cannot be kept (`incremental_ne_full_rebuild_of_objectiveId`), so `not_incremental_eq_full_rebuild` proves no theorem of the superseded shape exists and there was no strength there to preserve. The amended statement carries the clause's intent -- incremental update equals full rebuild from the same declaration base -- with the scope hypothesis REMOVED rather than assumed, and `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact` strengthens it past canonicalisation. A state produced by `Atlas.rebuild` is coherent (`rebuild_coherent`) and `Atlas.accumulate` preserves coherence (`semanticApplyBody_coherent`), so the coherence hypothesis excludes only hand-built states such as the counterexample's. The binding in Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean remains AMENDED and the SPEC 15 name remains OUTSTANDING -- now because the repository is SHORT of SPEC rather than ahead of it. Nothing here is counted as discharged.
deviations.amendmentText: ADOPTED. SPEC 12.5 now states rebuild equivalence in the state's own scope -- `Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))` -- over a state whose body is `Atlas.Coherent`, since `semanticRebuildBody` provably cannot reproduce a scope its only input does not name; and it requires `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact`, `semanticApplyBody_coherent` and `rebuild_coherent` beside it.

deviations.issue: THE DEFECT IS IN THE PINNED SPECIFICATION, NOT IN SPEC.md AND NOT IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION. This is the first deviation filed against the VENDORED Core 3.0 source rather than against SPEC.md's own text. The left-to-right direction of SPEC 7.3's biconditional is FALSE against the declarative side as pinned, and this is PROVED, not argued. `Instrs_ok/seq` of `vendor/wasm-spec/specification/wasm-3.0/2.3-validation.instructions.spectec` types the HEAD instruction with the principal relation `Instr_ok` and requires the TAIL's domain to be EXACTLY the head's codomain. The only rules that can adjust a type are `Instrs_ok/sub`, which preserves domain length because `Resulttype_sub` is a synchronised iteration over both sequences, and `Instrs_ok/frame`, which only makes a domain LONGER; both apply to SEQUENCES, and there is no `Instr_ok/sub` and no `Instr_ok/frame` anywhere in the vendored tree. A head that produces fewer operands than the tail consumes therefore can never be composed. `(I32.CONST c) (BINOP I32 ADD)` is the smallest instance: the pinned rules give it NO instruction type in ANY context, so no function body performing binary arithmetic is `Expr_ok`, no module containing one is `Module_ok`, and `DeclarativelyValid` as pinned is close to vacuous while `Wasm.validate` (which implements the appendix algorithm) accepts such modules. THE PINNED SOURCE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS POINT: `vendor/wasm-spec/document/core/valid/instructions.rst:1357-1366`, at the SAME commit, says the derivation exists and attributes the weakening of `eps -> I32` to `I32 -> I32 I32` to subsumption; that is not an `Instrtype_sub` supertype (the lengths differ), it is `Instrs_ok/frame` applied to the singleton SEQUENCE, a step `seq` cannot consume because its head premise is `Instr_ok`. Rendered prose cannot distinguish `Instr_ok` from `Instrs_ok` -- both print as `C |- ... : it` -- which is why the gap is invisible in the published document and bites only a mechanisation. UPSTREAM AGREES, AFTER THE PIN: WebAssembly/spec issue #2194 ('instrs_ok/seq's principality requirement is slightly over-restrictive', raoxiaojia, 2026-06-22) reports it in the same terms, and PR #2197 ('[spec] Fix instr sequence typing rules to actually be composable') merged the repair as commit bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008 on 2026-06-23 -- nine months after the pinned commit 9d36019973201a19f9c9ebb0f10828b2fe2374aa (2025-09-26). The vendored file is byte-identical to upstream blob bfd71e57ff457c61f546e0a308b99740fda02158 at the pin, so the transcription is not at fault; and the argument is about LENGTHS alone, so no operand-order or list-orientation convention in this repository could create or remove it.

deviations.resolution: The pin is NOT advanced: advancing past bd4633a would change the vendored blob set and the Core 3.0 rule inventory (it adds an `Instrs_ok/instr` rule and carries unrelated deltas). Instead the repository states the corrected hierarchy exactly once, in `WasmGemmGnaf/Wasm/Core/Validation/InstructionsCombinedAmended.lean` and `ModulesCombinedAmended.lean`, and carries this entry as its written justification. THE AMD-005 CHANGE IS ONE MODIFIED PREMISE AND NO NEW RULE: `Instrs_okA/seq` carries the frame `t_0*` INSIDE the composition -- `C |- instr_1 instr_2* : (t_0* t_1*) ->_(x_1* x_2*) t_3*` from `Instr_okA: C |- instr_1 : t_1* ->_(x_1*) t_2*`, `Resulttype_okA: C |- t_0* : OK` and `Instrs_okA: ... |- instr_2* : (t_0* t_2*) ->_(x_2*) t_3*`. `empty`, `sub` and `frame` are unchanged, and `t_0* = eps` is exactly the pinned rule. This is the frame the classic prose rule for instruction sequences already carries ('there is a sequence of value types t_0* such that t_2* = t_0* t*') and the second of the two repairs issue #2194 proposes; upstream took the first (lift the head to `Instrs_ok`, adding a rule and making `seq`'s subject an append that no longer determines the split). Because `Instr_ok/block`, `Instr_ok/loop` and `Instr_ok/if` type their bodies with the sequence judgment, the change is propagated through them by the mutual `Instr_okA`; otherwise the vacuity would survive one nesting level down. NO COVERAGE MARKER is attached to any corrected declaration, so the Core 3.0 inventory stays at 1288 of 1288 with validation rules 256 of 256. `Wasm.validate_iff_declarative` remains OUTSTANDING and is NOT counted as discharged; it SHALL be stated over `Module_okA` with this entry cited, never over the pinned relation.

deviations.amendmentText: ADOPTED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT AS A CHANGE TO `validate_bool_iff`. The earlier reading of this entry -- that SPEC.md needed no amendment at all -- was too narrow. The theorem needed none, but SPEC.md was silent on the defect, and silence in a normative document is an instruction: a reader following SPEC 7.3 as it stood would have validated against a pinned relation this repository has proved cannot type `i32.const c; i32.add`, and would have believed a near-vacuous `Module_ok` was the contract. AMD-005 therefore records, in SPEC 4 and SPEC 7.3: that the pinned WebAssembly Core revision carries this upstream defect; that the pin SHALL NOT be advanced on account of it, because advancing past bd4633a would change the vendored blob set and the rule inventory, which SPEC 4 makes a new-profile event; that `Wasm.DeclarativelyValid` SHALL be read over the sole combined amended `Instr_okA`/`Instrs_okA`/`Expr_okA`/`Func_okA`/`Module_okA` hierarchy; that the AMD-005 change SHALL be one modified premise and no new rule, propagated through nested control so the vacuity does not survive one nesting level down; that it SHALL carry explicit non-vacuity and arity evidence; that no coverage marker SHALL be attached to a corrected declaration, so the Core 3.0 inventory keeps measuring the PINNED tree; and that `validate_bool_iff` SHALL be stated over `Module_okA` with this entry cited, and remains OUTSTANDING. The substantive repair still belongs UPSTREAM and upstream has already made it: WebAssembly/spec PR #2197 (bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008). The pin is kept and this entry is carried.

deviations.issue: The pinned opcode-275 binary production constructs `VEXTTERNOP (I32 X 4) (I16 X 8) RELAXED_DOT_ADD S`. The independently transcribed operator-family premise requires `4 * lsize(input) = lsize(result) = 32`; after the instruction syntax's documented reversed family indexing, the pinned production demands the false equation `4 * 16 = 32`. It therefore constructs an instruction rejected by `Instr.wf` and whose numeric intermediate shape is not a 128-bit vector.
deviations.resolution: The release binary relation, decoder, and encoder replace only opcode 275's malformed second shape with `I8 X 16`, yielding `.vextternop ishI32x4 ishI8x16 (.relaxedDotAdd .s)`, and exclude the malformed pinned `I16 X 8` result. The byte-identical pinned relation and default remain unchanged.

amendments.was: SPEC 5 specified Lean tooling under Tools/ (Main.lean, EmitArtifact.lean, GenerateManifest.lean, GenerateConformance.lean, CheckClaims.lean, CheckAxioms.lean, CheckSources.lean, Reproduce.lean) and stated: 'The Rust workspace ... SHALL be removed after the Lean conformance replacement passes. No Rust code is part of the final product or proof path.'
amendments.now: SPEC 5.1 'Language boundary' fixes two languages. Lean 4 is the proof and implementation language: every definition, theorem, semantics, cost model, plan, compiler and artifact-producing term lives under WasmGemmGnaf/ and is checked by the Lean kernel. Rust is the infrastructure and tooling language: the release gate, source and firewall scans, claim and axiom audits, manifest and documentation generators, mutation suite and reproduction driver live under xtask/ and are driven by the Justfile.
amendments.rationale: Requested by the repository owner. The boundary preserves the property the original clause protected: the trust base stays the Lean kernel. xtask CHECKS whether the kernel has discharged an obligation; it never DECIDES one. A tool that decided a proof obligation would move the trust base outside the kernel, which SPEC 4 forbids.
constraintsAdded: The boundary is one-directional: nothing under WasmGemmGnaf/ may depend on xtask.
No Rust code is on the proof path.
xtask SHALL build with the Rust standard library alone -- a network-fetched crate would be a network-fetched input to release verification, which SPEC 4 forbids.
Rust source SHALL NOT appear under WasmGemmGnaf/, and Lean source SHALL NOT appear under xtask/.
amendments.supersedes: DEV-003 (never filed; the deviation was amended into the SPEC instead)

amendments.was: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation
amendments.now: theorem costed_erase_iff_plain_run : Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation <-> (Wasm.Run module invocation (eraseCosts costedTrace) observation /\ Wasm.CostedLabelling module invocation costedTrace), with `theorem costed_run_iff_plain_run : (exists costedTrace, Wasm.CostedRun P module invocation costedTrace observation) <-> Wasm.Run module invocation observation.trace observation` required beside it and `Wasm.CostedLabelling` defined in the same fenced block.
amendments.rationale: The superseded text is KERNEL-REFUTED, for every profile, by `WasmGemmGnaf.Wasm.not_costed_erase_iff_plain_run`. A normative document that states a proposition this repository has proved false instructs its readers to prove something impossible, so the text is corrected rather than deviated from. The added conjunct is the smallest change that makes the biconditional true: it is a condition on LABELS alone, mentioning no observation, no store and no terminal status, and it names exactly the payload information `eraseCosts` discards.
amendments.strengthEffect: STRENGTHENING. The forward direction is strictly stronger than the text it replaces; the backward direction is the strongest true form, since no theorem of the superseded shape exists.
amendments.ledgerEffect: HISTORICALLY, `Wasm.costed_erase_iff_plain_run` moved from OUTSTANDING to DISCHARGED when the formula amendment landed: SPEC 15 went 34 of 58 to 35 of 58 on zero new proof lines. That promotion is now reversed. The existing theorem is over legacy `Wasm.Subset.Module`, whereas SPEC's public carrier is amended-Core `Wasm.Module`; Conformance/RequiredSignatures.lean therefore marks it WEAKER and the name is OUTSTANDING. The amendment still repairs the false formula, but it closes no public-carrier proof obligation.

amendments.was: theorem incremental_eq_full_rebuild (hupdate : (Atlas.accumulate budget state delta).result = .complete successor) : Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBody (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations))
amendments.now: theorem incremental_eq_full_rebuild (hcoherent : Atlas.Coherent state.body) (hupdate : (Atlas.accumulate budget state delta).result = .complete successor) : Atlas.canonicalize successor.body = Atlas.canonicalize (Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith state.body.scope (state.body.declarationBase U delta.declarations)); with `incremental_eq_full_rebuild_exact`, `semanticApplyBody_coherent` and `rebuild_coherent` required beside it, and `Atlas.Coherent` and `Atlas.semanticRebuildBodyWith` defined in the clause's own fenced block.
amendments.rationale: The superseded text is KERNEL-REFUTED six ways by Atlas/Rebuild.lean, including that restricting it to unscoped states does not rescue it. The obvious repair -- adding BOTH load-bearing hypotheses, which is precisely the shape of the declaration already named `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` -- was REJECTED: amending SPEC to match a weaker theorem the repository happens to have is the failure mode this log exists to prevent. SPEC was amended to the STRONGER scope-free form instead, which fixes the scope objection by rebuilding in the state's own scope rather than assuming it away.
amendments.strengthEffect: STRENGTHENING. The amended statement implies the repaired literal one (instantiate the scope at `unscoped`) and additionally constrains every scoped state, about which the superseded text said nothing true. `Atlas.Coherent` is discharged rather than assumed, by the two coherence laws now required beside it.
amendments.ledgerEffect: NONE, AND THE GAP REVERSED DIRECTION. `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild` stays OUTSTANDING -- now because the declaration wearing the required name is WEAKER than SPEC asks, not stronger. The amended proposition is proved here as `Atlas.incremental_eq_full_rebuild_scoped`; the remaining action is a restatement under the required name in Atlas/Rebuild.lean, outside the files the amending change owned.

AMD-004 remains as an explicit record that the normative obligation was narrowed; it is not presented as a proved necessity and earns no release credit.
amendments.strengthEffect: THE OBLIGATION SHRANK, AND THIS ROW IS THE DISCLOSURE. The superseded clause quantified over every byte string; the amended one does not. Within the reduced scope the surviving theorem proves a conjunction stronger than the former disjunction. amendments.was: SPEC 4 recorded the WebAssembly Core pin with no note of any defect, and SPEC 7.3 required `validate_bool_iff` against `Wasm.DeclarativelyValid` without saying which validation relation that names.
amendments.now: SPEC 4 records that the pinned revision carries a known upstream defect in its instruction-sequence typing rule and that the pin SHALL NOT be advanced on account of it. SPEC 7.3 states the defect in full, and requires: `Wasm.DeclarativelyValid` read over the sole combined amended `Instr_okA`/`Instrs_okA`/`Expr_okA`/`Func_okA`/`Module_okA` hierarchy; the AMD-005 change to be one modified premise and no new rule, propagated through nested control; explicit non-vacuity and arity evidence; no coverage marker on any corrected declaration, so the Core 3.0 inventory keeps measuring the pinned tree; and `validate_bool_iff` stated over `Module_okA` with DEV-006 cited.
amendments.rationale: THE DEFECT IS IN THE VENDORED PINNED SOURCE, NOT IN SPEC.md AND NOT IN THE TRANSCRIPTION. `validate_bool_iff` is the right proposition and is UNCHANGED. What was wrong was SPEC's silence: a reader following SPEC 7.3 as it stood would have validated against a relation this repository has proved cannot type `i32.const c; i32.add`, under which no function body performing binary arithmetic is `Expr_ok` and `Module_ok` is near-vacuous. Upstream agrees, after the pin: WebAssembly/spec issue #2194 and PR #2197, merged as bd4633aced30b720ff62b44cf00c03ece792f008, nine months after the pinned commit 9d36019973201a19f9c9ebb0f10828b2fe2374aa.
amendments.strengthEffect: THE AMD-005 SEQUENCING RULE IS STRICTLY WIDER, BOUNDED AND DISCLOSED. It is composed with the independent AMD-007 through AMD-011 and AMD-013 corrections in one `A` hierarchy; AMD-012 separately repairs a binary production. This entry therefore does not assert global inclusion between the complete pinned and corrected relations. The ordinary arithmetic witnesses and re-proved arity invariants show that composability was bought by supplying operands from the frame and not by letting a binary operator consume fewer operands.
amendments.ledgerEffect: NONE. `Wasm.validate_iff_declarative` stays OUTSTANDING and CIRCULAR; the required conditional pinned-to-combined compatibility theorems at the Instr, Instrs, Expr, Func, and Module levels remain absent under WS-001; the Core 3.0 inventory is unchanged because no coverage marker is attached to an amended declaration; and the pin in authority/manifest.json is not moved.

amendments.was: SPEC 11.1 listed loop nests among the constructs a plan represents and stated no rule for the trip count of a register-bounded loop.
amendments.now: A loop whose trip count is read from a register SHALL clamp that count at the profile's address-space ceiling (`Plan.loopRegMaxTrips = 2^32 - 1`, the released i32 ceiling, equal to `maxRawExtent`), so that a static step bound remains derivable from the plan text alone; the trip count is still exactly the memory word below the ceiling.
amendments.rationale: An unclamped register-bounded loop would falsify `Plan.steps_le_stepBound`, which bounds executed steps by a Nat computed from the plan text; no fixed number bounds a loop whose trip count is an arbitrary register value.
amendments.strengthEffect: NEUTRAL IN REACH. The ceiling equals `maxRawExtent` and is unreachable for any configuration the released ABI can present or any value the compiled i32 locals can hold. The clamp preserves an existing theorem instead of weakening one.
amendments.ledgerEffect: NONE. No SPEC 15 name is affected.
